sections.h2: What choices does a Richardson, TX seller have?
sections.html:
A Richardson owner can list the house, sell it privately, or accept an as-is cash purchase. The right one depends on repairs, timing and how much of the sale price you need to keep.

Richardson is an established inner-ring suburb north of Dallas that spans Dallas County and Collin County. Many of its houses are older, which can make an as-is sale attractive when a roof, foundation or kitchen needs work you do not want to fund. The city even runs a program meant to push owners to reinvest in older homes, covered below, which tells you how the city sees its aging housing stock.

  • List with an agent: most exposure, with repair negotiations after inspection.
  • Private sale: no listing fee, but you manage buyer screening and paperwork.
  • As-is cash sale: you skip repairs and showings and set the closing date.

sections.h2: Which county tax office bills a Richardson house?
sections.html:
It depends on which county the property sits in. The City of Richardson's property tax page says taxes must be paid at the county tax office where the property is located, and it lists both offices.

Appraisals come from the Dallas Central Appraisal District for Dallas County addresses and the Collin Central Appraisal District for Collin ones. DCAD says it appraises for 61 local governing bodies in the county and reported more than 250,000 protests for 2026, so hearings ran long. If you plan to protest next year, file early and ask for an informal review with an appraiser.

sections.h2: Does Richardson have a program that rewards home improvements?
sections.html:
Yes. The city's Home Improvement Incentive Program pays a one-time incentive to owners who remodel or rebuild a single-family home. For buyers, a house that already went through the program may have a higher appraised value.

  • The project must cost at least $20,000 and finish within 24 months of approval.
  • You apply to Community Services before construction starts.
  • The payment equals 10 times the increase in city taxes, based on the appraisal district's certified values.
  • Owners who are delinquent in taxes or fees are not eligible.

The incentive is paid on April 1 of the first full calendar year after the project is done. Community Services can be reached at 972-744-4166, and the city notes the payment may have federal income tax effects. If you are about to sell, a remodel started now will not repay you before closing, so this program suits owners who plan to stay.

sections.h2: What schools and commuting options matter in Richardson?
sections.html:
Richardson is served mainly by Richardson ISD, with parts of the city in Plano ISD. The city's school page says RISD covers 46 square miles in Dallas County across parts of Richardson, Dallas and Garland, with more than 36,000 students on 50 campuses.

Plano ISD covers about 100 square miles in southwest Collin County, including northern parts of Richardson. Which district your house falls in is a real pricing factor, so confirm it with the district before you advertise.

Higher education is close: the University of Texas at Dallas opened in 1969, and Dallas College Richland Campus and Collin College are both listed on the city's page. For commuters, the city lists DART rail, Trinity Railway Express and bus service, plus NTTA tollways. Proximity to rail is a selling point you can state plainly in a listing.

sections.h2: How do Texas tax rules apply when a Richardson house sells?
sections.html:
Your tax lien attached on January 1 for the year, and taxes for the part of the year you owned the home are settled at closing. Bills go out around October 1.

  • Most owners must pay by January 31; February 1 begins delinquency.
  • Penalty and interest start at six and one percent, and the penalty climbs to 12 percent on July 1.
  • Owners 65 or older or disabled can pay in installments.
  • A 10 percent annual cap applies to appraised value on a homestead.

The school homestead exemption is $140,000, and a disabled veteran exemption ranges by disability rating, with a full exemption on a homestead for 100 percent disabled veterans. Ask the appraisal district what exemptions are on your account before you set a net-proceeds target.

sections.h2: What if a Richardson owner is behind on payments or inherited the house?
sections.html:
Texas lenders can use non-judicial foreclosure, which means a short timeline. You have 20 days after the notice of default to reinstate, the notice of sale must come at least 21 days before the auction, and sales occur on the first Tuesday of the month.

For inherited houses, the paperwork route depends on how the estate is handled. A will can be probated within four years of death. A small estate affidavit requires assets of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead, and an affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement filed with the county clerk that third parties are not required to accept. If the owner left a transfer on death deed, record the affidavit of death and death certificate.

The deed itself is recorded with the clerk of the county where Richardson's property lies; the clerk manual lists $5.00 for a first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus other small fees.

faqs.q: Do I pay Richardson property tax to the city or the county?
faqs.a: The city's own page says taxes are paid at the county tax office where the property is located. Use the Dallas County or Collin County office listed above for your address.

faqs.q: Is Richardson in Dallas County or Collin County?
faqs.a: Both. The city spans the two counties, and the city's tax page lists a tax office for each.

faqs.q: What is the minimum cost for Richardson's home improvement incentive?
faqs.a: A project must cost at least $20,000 and be completed within 24 months of approval. Apply to Community Services before construction begins.
Richardson ISD and Plano ISD. RISD spans 46 square miles in Dallas County, and Plano ISD includes northern parts of Richardson in Collin County.

faqs.q: When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1, for most bills unpaid by January 31. The collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest at that point.
